crime_highlights: The accused pled guilty to committing manslaughter to Deborah Joseph, his common law wife.
She was stabbed in the heart by the accused.
The accused was so drunk at the time of, and shortly after, the killing that he has no memory of the killing.
rationale_highlights: The accused is a 50-year old Aboriginal person who is an Indian Residential School survivor.
I have to consider the accused's tragic Aboriginal background and the impact that background has had on his moral culpability for committing this offence
I also have to ensure that the sentence that I impose on this accused does not lead inadvertently to discrimination in sentencing.
note: Court never states the background reduced the sentence.

crime_highlights: Ms. Quilt assaulted a woman named Shaina Solomon
she kicked her a couple of times, tossed her to the floor
she uttered a threat that she would do physical harm to Ms. Solomon
Ms. Quilt went in and attacked them with a knife
serious injuries were suffered by both of those persons
rationale_highlights: Her parents and grandparents had been subjected to the residential school experience
Ms. Quilt was exposed to substantial substance abuse, particularly alcohol abuse, as she was growing up.
I am well aware of the proposition that incarceration is to be applied sparingly, judiciously, and that special concerns apply with respect to Aboriginal offenders.
note: Court notes Aboriginal concerns but never states effect on sentence.

crime_highlights: The fire that damaged the residence at 2772 Merritt Road, Prince George, British Columbia, was deliberately set.
The deceased, Mr. Jawanda, died as a result of smoke inhalation which was caused by the fire.
The fire was started with the use of an accelerant which was poured on the mattresses in both bedrooms in the main floor suite.
Mr. Marion said that he was going to burn down the residence on December 11, 2011.
rationale_highlights: Mr. Marion clearly has suffered, as many First Nations persons who appear before these courts do, from substance abuse, lower educational attainment, lower income, high unemployment, and a high incidence of incarceration.
Mr. Marion has also suffered abuse during his childhood and exposure to alcoholism by his parents.
While I do take into account Mr. Marion's First Nations heritage and the above-noted factors
note: Heritage listed as mitigating but court says factors militate against non-custodial sentence.
